source: Schneider Electric press release: Schneider Electric unveils new prefabricated reference (10-21-2026)

players.product: EcoStruxure UPS, PDU, prefab modular datacenter blocks

quarterly_data.signal: Schneider Electric announced its RapidScale Modular Data Center Reference Design 115, a validated, pre-engineered blueprint for high-density AI infrastructure that brings together the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform and liquid cooling, validated to ANSI standards for U.S. deployments (IEC support planned); the company calls it a first step toward supporting the NVIDIA DSX POD reference design. RapidScale, its prefabricated modular data center portfolio, incorporates approximately 90% in-house manufactured equipment. Schneider says the manufacturing capacity behind it has grown fourfold since 2025 and spans eight primary sites totaling 1.35 million square feet, plus three additional facilities and 12 partner sites across 10 countries.
quarterly_data.figure: manufacturing capacity grown fourfold since 2025; eight primary sites totaling 1.35 million square feet; approximately 90% in-house manufactured equipment
quarterly_data.quarter: Schneider Electric press release: Schneider Electric unveils new prefabricated reference (10-21-2026)

quarterly_data.signal: White Paper 238, co-authored with Compass Datacenters from a time study at a Compass hyperscale data center campus: prefabricated modular white-space pods cut onsite installation from 75.5 hours to 15 hours per pod, an 80% reduction. Schneider estimates global data center capacity will increase by 170 GW by 2030 to 300 GW in total (2.3 times the 2025 installed base), with AI workloads expected to account for approximately 65% of demand by the end of the decade.
quarterly_data.figure: 75.5 to 15 hours per pod (80% reduction); +170 GW to 300 GW by 2030 (company estimate)
